task.intro: You have been given a task by the Overseers. Pick one:

options.title: Guide
options.descriptionText: You are meant to guide people towards a desired end. What is it?

options.title: Herald
options.descriptionText: You are meant to bring instructions to other people. What do you teach?

options.title: Watcher
options.descriptionText: You are meant to search for signs of something. What are the signs?

options.title: Witness
options.descriptionText: You are meant to record and observe ongoing events. What do you record?

secretWisdom.description: You've received insight from your Task. At the start of each session, roll +Cool. On a 10+, hold 2. On a 7-9, hold 1. On a miss, hold 1, but the Keeper introduces a cruel choice or terrible truth related to your Task. Hold can be spent in different ways based on your Task:

effectText.title: Guide
effectText.descriptionText: When you advise as instructed by the Overseers, spend 1 hold to help out without needing to be in the same place, or spend 2 hold to help out on a start-of-mystery or start-of-session move.

effectText.title: Herald
effectText.descriptionText: When you announce your Overseers’ demands, spend 1 hold to manipulate a monster, if it is capable of communication.

effectText.title: Watcher
effectText.descriptionText: When you examine the patterns of Fate, spend 1 hold to protect someone even when you are not in the same place.

effectText.title: Witness
effectText.descriptionText: When you report to the Overseers, spend 1 hold to grant any hunter one question as if they just investi- gated a mystery.

overseers.intro: The Envoy was sent or given a task by a higher power. Describe your Overseers according to their Values and your Concerns.
overseers.trailing: The Envoy doesn't have a means to contact their Overseers easily in the way the Initiate and Professional can. This is by design--the Overseers are hands-off and esoteric compared to an Agency or Sect. You can use magic to reach out, otherwise contact is always at the Overseers' whim.

values.detail: PRESENT, but rendered differently from Curse-eater's inline convention: "Something else:" is its own text item (ending the line); the underscore run is a SEPARATE text item on the NEXT line, left-aligned to the same x as the label (not appended inline after the colon on the same line). Exactly 21 consecutive underscore characters, plain/regular font, no leading/trailing whitespace in the item itself.

concerns.detail: PRESENT, identical rendering convention and identical length to the Values blank marker: same 21-underscore run as its own text item on the line below "Something else:", left-aligned under the label at its own x-column (x=172.27 for Concerns vs x=49.5 for Values — different sub-column, same pattern). Confirmed independently rather than assumed identical from Values' finding.

formattingNote: Page 17: Task's 4 options are fully plain (bold titles only, no additional inline formatting). Secret Wisdom's Description has 1 italic span ("At the start of each session") not predicted. Secret Wisdom's EffectText has 1 italic + 1 bold span per entry (4 entries — 4 italic, 5 bold spans total, since Guide's entry has 2 separate bold "help out" spans). Page 18: Overseers' intro and trailing paragraphs are plain except one bold cross-reference ("use magic") in the trailing paragraph; all 21 Values+Concerns tag labels are plain (confirmed 0 collisions). A false positive was found and fixed during this pass: the bold "Overseers" section heading collided with the ordinary word "Overseers" appearing in both prose blocks — fixed by narrowing the Y bound to exclude the heading.
